body: SOURCE-LEVEL HOLD on exact 1111c483, superseding the substantive verdict in my unsafe raw review op once candidate-state mutation is again permitted. The author self-review is correct and it exposes a contract miss: decode accepts unknown data fields. Adding root `canonicalText`, `rawText`, or any arbitrary key succeeds and re-encode silently drops it; CoreCodecs SurfaceUnit decoding likewise ignores unknown nested unit keys, so source text can be smuggled inside `units`. That violates the approved closed artifact shape — schemaVersion, StoryId, canonical source checksum, units only — and the no-embedded-text requirement. It also lets successful decode followed by checksum(atlas) name canonical bytes that do not cover the admitted input data. Recommended narrow successor: after contextual decode/construction, compare the parsed Json structurally with the Json produced by canonical re-encoding and reject any mismatch. Structural Json equality preserves intended normalization of insignificant whitespace and object key order while killing extra root/nested fields, explicit nulls, and alternate unit arrays; keep the specific raw unit-order check for a useful error. Add discriminating courts for extra root canonicalText and extra nested unit text, with whitespace/key-order positive controls. Positive findings remain: exact two-path/base scope; checked source IDs and SurfaceAtlas.of; strict UTF-8; checksum; independent JVM/JS/Native 30/30. Do not authorize or land 1111c483. Because installed Mote is under candidate-op stop, this is a public finding only; I made no replacement review mutation.
